guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our view shades toward Army because its rushing production has been both efficient and varied. Army averaged 394 rushing yards through two games and produced 25 runs of at least 10 yards, while operating behind a listed starting offensive line made up entirely of seniors. We are not treating that early production as proof, but the combination of experience and multiple rushing threats helps explain why our numbers are slightly more favorable to Army than the market.

We also see enough resistance to keep this from becoming a wager. Tulsa allowed 3.1 yards per carry through four games, and our matchup numbers identify Tulsa's own rushing offense and scoring-opportunity creation as potential problems for Army. The early raw results say Army allowed only 98.5 rushing yards and 15.5 points per game, but our efficiency profile is less convinced by its scoring-opportunity prevention. For us, those competing matchup strengths leave a genuine disagreement with the market, but not enough value at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
The matchup we are watching is Army's rushing offense against Tulsa's defensive front. Tulsa used the same front-seven starters in each of its first four games, with Chris Thompson Jr. and Dax Collins leading the team in tackles. That continuity and early run-defense production provide a meaningful test for Army's experienced offensive line.

We think Tulsa's ability to limit productive early-down runs will shape the game. If Army consistently stays on schedule, its multidimensional ground game can control possessions; if Tulsa creates longer-yardage situations, the market's preference for the home team becomes easier to justify.

recent_game.fact: Army lost 28-24 to South Florida on Sept. 12, leaving the Black Knights 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Against South Florida, Cale Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns; his .900 completion percentage was a career high.
Godspower Nwawuihe led Army against South Florida with 20 carries for 98 yards and scored a 10-yard fourth-quarter rushing touchdown.
Zach Mundell caught three passes against South Florida, including a 24-yard touchdown from Cale Hellums, and completed a 37-yard pass to Godspower Nwawuihe.

quarterback.fact: Senior Cale Hellums is listed as Army's starting quarterback, followed by sophomore Bryson Luter and sophomore Ethan Washington.
Hellums returned as Army's starter in 2026 after making 10 starts and appearing in every game in 2025.
Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025; the touchdown total was second in Army single-season history.
Through two 2026 games, Hellums had 150 passing yards, 142 rushing yards and four total touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Army's listed starting offensive line is left tackle Henry Appleton, left guard Kyle Kloska, center Brady Small, right guard Paolo Gennarelli and right tackle Teddy Williams; all five are seniors.

Nwawuihe emerged as Army's feature back in 2026 after a breakout performance in the 2025 Fenway Bowl.
